rows.name: Field Separator
rows.comment: Field separators are not used in FHIR.

rows.name: Encoding Characters
rows.comment: Encoding characters are not used in FHIR.

rows.name: Sending Application
rows.comment: We believe that if MSH-24 is vaued, although MSH-24 is rarely valued, it contains better information for the MessageHeader.source.endpoint than MSH-3. However, one may either still want to use MSH-3 in total or a combination of content from MSH-3 and MSH-24. That is a local implementation decision to adjust the mapping accordingly based on clear knowledge of the content. If both MSH-3 and MSH-24 are not valued, which is valid in HL7 v2, then the implementer needs to resolve how to assign MessageHeader.source as it is a required attribute. Note that a data absent reason extension could be used to provide a reason and satisfy the mandatory FHIR attribute rules. But do note that the use of the data-absent-reason extension may result in a FHIR resource that is not usable by the recipient.

rows.name: Receiving Application
rows.comment: Similar as for MSH-3, MSH-5 is paired with MSH-25 and depending on local use may need to use one, the other, or a combination of both. We believe that MSH-25, when valued, provides the better information given its addition to the standard more recently.

rows.name: Date/Time of Message
rows.comment: If a message is always conveyed in a Bundle, then Bundle.timestamp could work. However, Bundle.timestamp may be better used to reflect the conversion. See https://chat.fhir.org/#narrow/stream/179188-v2-to.20FHIR/topic/MessageHeader.2Etimestamp for a discussion on this topic.

rows.name: Message Control ID
rows.comment: Need a gForge to request a MessageHeader.identifier (https://gforge.hl7.org/gf/project/fhir/tracker/?action=TrackerItemEdit&tracker_item_id=20704&start=0) Note that if a message is part of a batch, then the MSH goes to a "sub-bundle".. Note that as messages switch from V2 to FHIR and the response back from FHIR to V2, the "mapping engine" needs to track the actual MSH.10.00.00 value and Bundle.identifier value to connect responses correctly.

rows.name: Version ID
rows.comment: We agreed that the version of the v2 message that was used to transform into FHIR is addressed through Provenance. Either the Provenance instance representing the original message can include in Provenance.entity.what a binary of the total original message, or the proposed MessageHeader.identifier containing MSH-10 provides the link to the original message.

rows.name: Continuation Pointer
rows.comment: There is no continuation pointer concept in FHIR. When a continuation is used, the mapper needs to continue to obtain the additional data that is defined in the mappings.

rows.name: Accept Acknowledgment Type
rows.comment: This field is not mapped as there is no continuation of a system level acknowledgement request beyond the mapping engine. Any subsequent acknowledgement methods would be performed in the applicable subsequent transport methods.

rows.name: Application Acknowledgment Type
rows.comment: Interacting with the recipient on what type/level or validation is asked to be reported and it is not yet clear what the appropriate mechanism is, e.g., using interactions using Task (as it is more application level interactions) and/or HTTP header and/or other mechanisms. Note that the MSH-16 values are typically pre-determined through an implementation guide. Until then we encourage implementers to share feedback on how they are planning to address this that we can consider for inclusion

rows.name: Principal Language Of Message
rows.comment: This does only cover the MessageHeader resource. Need to have clarity that if other resources that are part of the message that do not have Resource.meta.language valued, then it is assumed to follow MessageHeader.meta.language?? Doesn't seem RESTful, so what is the default for Resource.meta.language?

rows.name: Message Profile Identifier
rows.comment: Need to support multiple profiles. Also, comment on implicitRules is highly idealistic.

rows.name: Receiving Responsible Organization
rows.comment: This is an alternate representation of MSH-6. The local implementation needs to determine whech components of HD vs. XON to be used and whether it may even yield a separate Organization reference.

rows.name: Sending Network Address

However, one may either still want to use MSH-3 in total or a combination of content from MSH-3 and MSH-24. That is a local implementation decision to adjust the mapping accordingly.
